Hello World

Your first Ifá-Lang program

Welcome to Ifá-Lang!

Every programming journey starts with a simple program that displays "Hello, World!" on the screen. In Ifá-Lang, we use the Irosu domain for console output.

The Code

Here's your first Ifá-Lang program:

// hello.ifa - Your first Ifá program
Irosu.fo("Kaabo, Ifá!");

Let's break it down:

  • // - A comment, ignored by the interpreter
  • Irosu - The Console I/O domain (Odu pattern: 1100)
  • .fo() - The "print line" method (short for "fọ̀rọ̀" = speak)
  • "Kaabo, Ifá!" - A string to display (Yoruba for "Welcome, Ifá!")
Bilingual Aliases

Ifá-Lang supports both Yoruba and English. You can also write:

Irosu.println("Hello, Ifá!");

Running Your Program

Save the code to a file called hello.ifa, then run:

ifa run hello.ifa

Output:

Kaabo, Ifá!

More Output Methods

Irosu has several output methods:

// Print with newline
Irosu.fo("Line 1");
Irosu.fo("Line 2");

// Print without newline
Irosu.so("Hello, ");
Irosu.so("World!");
Irosu.fo("");  // Add newline

// Print an error message (to stderr)
Irosu.kigbe("Something went wrong!");

What You Learned

  • How to create an Ifá-Lang source file (.ifa)
  • How to print output using Irosu.fo()
  • That Ifá-Lang is bilingual (Yoruba + English aliases)
  • How to run a program with ifa run
